text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - German debt recovered from early losses to trade slightly higher late in the day as dealers covered short-positions taken ahead of French elections over the weekend. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.82, up 0/13 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts were at session low after money supply, credit data, with UK M0 money supply up prov s/a 6.1 percent in year to May, v 6.5 pct forecast. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 112-23/32, up 03/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond and interest rate futures confounded predictions they would slide if Socialist-led government, including the Communists, won in Sunday's parliamentary election. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.52, up 0.02 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian Btp futures moved up into positive territory above 128.80 resistance, following other debt markets and helped by stronger lire, but operators uncertain of strength of rally and still awaiting moves in Bundesbank/Bonn gold row. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.20, up 0.30 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries stayed moderately lower in late-morning trade, with players report retail selling, mainly at short end after NAPM, treasuries still holding most of last week's gains, hedge fund buying. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-30/32, down 03/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.92 percent.

JAPAN - The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended slightly lower in the face of firm Tokyo stocks and an impending shift of the benchmark from June to September. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 123.86, down 0.33 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market activity was dominated by TMCC's $1.0 billion 10-year Euro-asian offering and Turkey's plans for a 1.0 billion mark five-year bond. The TMCC deal will be priced later at a 23 b.p. spread. Turkey awarded Commerzbank and WestLB the mandate for a mark bond shortly after announcing it will hold its next election early.
